## Today

1. **Quiz 6** (25 minutes)
2. **Project session** (remaining time): one short activity with your project group, then work time.

::: {.notes}
For the TA. Quiz 6 first, 25 minutes; collect the quizzes before starting the activity. Then about 50 minutes: 5 for deadlines, 15 for the activity and share-out, and about 30 of supervised work time. Students should sit with their project groups after the quiz.
:::

Instructions: [presentation](../project/presentation.qmd), [peer review](../project/peer-review.qmd), [report](../project/report.qmd), [evaluations](../project/evaluations.qmd).

## Checking Your Own Project

On your own for 2 minutes, then as a group for 8:

1. What is your **descriptive model**, and your **method**?
2. Which **single assumption** would most change your recommendation?
3. Which **check** would reveal it: refining, validating, sensitivity, robustness?
4. **Who is affected** if it's wrong?

::: {.notes}
About 10 minutes. Circulate and push for specifics. An example answer, for a multi-objective water management project: (1) a reservoir mass balance driven by historical inflows, searched for release rules that trade off supply against environmental flows; (2) that future inflows look like the historical record; (3) robustness: test the chosen rules across drier inflow scenarios, or a sensitivity analysis on the inflow distribution; (4) the downstream ecosystem and the irrigators who would be cut first. If a group says "no assumption would change our answer", ask what they held fixed that they could not measure.
:::

## Your Report's Discussion Section

> [Discussion and Conclusions] ... including how assumptions made in your project may have influenced the results or their interpretation as well as reflections on how your project connected to or extended the course material.

Answers to questions 2–4 are a **first draft of that paragraph**: write it down before you leave.

::: {.notes}
Point at the quote: this is word for word from the report instructions. The activity is ungraded; its purpose is a paragraph the group can build on. Posting to Ed is optional and ungraded, but it gets them feedback before the deadline.
:::

## Share Out

Two or three groups, one minute each:

- The **assumption** that would most change your recommendation.
- The **check** that would reveal it.

::: {.notes}
About 5 minutes. Pick groups with different kinds of projects. Patterns worth pointing out: many projects rest on an input distribution taken from history, or on a cost or efficiency number from one source; the matching checks are robustness across other futures and a sensitivity analysis over a defensible range.
:::

## Work Time

The rest of class: work with your group on the **video** and the **report**. Ask the TA as you go.

Optional: post your draft Discussion paragraph to Ed (ungraded) for comments before Dec 20.

::: {.notes}
About 30 minutes. Circulate; most groups will be editing videos or drafting the report. If course evaluations are open, take 5 minutes for them at the start of this block. End a few minutes early with a reminder that the video is due tomorrow at 9:00 PM.
:::
